# REQ-604 AC-1 golden event sequence for one turn that raises a consent prompt,
# is answered, and dispatches. The second of the two scenarios REQ-599 AC-6
# named and never captured.
#
# PROVENANCE (load-bearing): captured at `17c39ec`, where the turn path is
# still the pre-split single-file `crates/tetond/src/runtime.rs` and no
# *runtime* `TurnContext` exists. A fixture regenerated at tip would be an
# oracle computed by the subject (conventions.md; LESSON-569).
#
# base commit: 17c39ec4f26432fae22bfb4d266159ce8afb614f
#
# "no *runtime* TurnContext" is deliberate — see the sibling skill fixture's
# header for why the unqualified claim would be slightly too strong.
#
# The scenario: a plain typed prompt whose scripted reply is a `shell` tool
# call. The gate raises `permission_request`, the harness answers it
# `allow_once`, and the turn runs on to a final answer. The answer is awaited on
# the event, never on a timer (LESSON-450).
#
# Note the two `prefix_cache` entries: this turn makes two engine calls — the
# one that produces the tool call, and the one that produces the final answer
# after the gate is answered — and each reports its own cache outcome. That the
# consent prompt falls *between* them is the ordering this fixture exists to
# pin.
#
# FORMAT: one event per line, in publication order. Consecutive runs of the same
# event collapse to one entry (the trailing `session_update session_update` of
# the dispatch stream is one entry here). `route_decided` carries its category,
# because that is the discriminator both sides filter on.
#
# DETACHED ENTRIES — excluded by discriminator, never by position (AC-4,
# LESSON-591):
#
#   route_decided[category=title]  the title duty's own decision
#   session_titled                 the naming task's result
#
# Across 144 capture runs of this scenario at this commit the raw order was
# stable, but stability across 144 runs on one machine is not a property — it is
# the exact evidence LESSON-591 warns is insufficient, since that race passed
# 40/40 locally and on `ubuntu-latest` and went red only on `macos-latest`. The
# two entries are dropped by discriminator because of what publishes them, not
# because they were seen to move here.
route_decided[category=edit]
route_decided[category=title]
session_titled
prefix_cache
session_update
permission_request
session_update
prefix_cache
